lot.source: EVAL STAND-IN, not from the drawings: a rectangle 20 ft clear of the house's sides and 30 ft front and back. Check my project sends nothing without a property line and a street edge (ProjectFacts), and the repository has no survey of Lot 2. Every zoning row of the check is Ithaca's, which doesn't apply in Orangetown, and is left out of the comparison; no egress rule reads the lot (egress.check reads the interior and the dwelling units only)

plan: x east from the house's west outer face, y north from its south-most face (the garage front), feet (layout.yaml's x, and d turned: y = (508 in - d) / 12); z 0 the second floor's finished floor

not_drawn.stairs: house.yaml has no stairs: 'No floor-to-floor height is dimensioned, so no riser height or nosing elevation can be placed, and no tread depth is dimensioned' (layout.yaml not_drawn.stairs places them only). Every stair rule stays needs review (evaluation.md, why D)
not_drawn.guards: house.yaml's 5 railings have no members ('drawn ... but not dimensioned', absent.members): not drawn (layout.yaml not_drawn.guards). The guard rules read open sides, which nothing produces yet (evaluation.md, why G), so drawing them would change no verdict
not_drawn.interior doors, sliders, garage doors, m: layout.yaml assumptions: house.yaml describes only the front door and the marked escape windows; a drawn door is read as a door

assumptions.what: Floor-to-floor heights (main floor 118.5 in, basement 108 in below the main floor)
assumptions.why: not dimensioned (A-4 gives floor-to-ceiling heights only); answer_key.yaml's framing reading
assumptions.effect: none: no stair is drawn, and no measure in scope compares levels

assumptions.what: Each floor slab drawn as thick as the gap the layout leaves under it: the second floor's 10.5 in (2x10 joists, subfloor and board), the main floor's 12 in (2x12 joists and subfloor, A-5); the basement's 4 in concrete (A-2)
assumptions.why: a slab thicker than the gap would cut into the cited ceiling below it (A-4's 9'-0" main floor)
assumptions.effect: none: every ceiling is drawn where A-4 puts it, and no slab reaches below one

assumptions.what: Each window pair drawn 2 in apart (`pair_gap`), centred on the pair's dimensioned centre
assumptions.why: the plans show mulled pairs with one centre dimension; each unit is its own family, so they are kept from overlapping
assumptions.effect: none: no window has a clear opening to measure

assumptions.what: Bedroom 4's 10'-0" x 1'-4" window recess left out; its windows drawn in the straight south wall at d 466-472
assumptions.why: house.yaml leaves the recess out (no inside dimension: its 10'-0" and 1'-4" are outside dimensions), and its windows must open from bedroom 4
assumptions.effect: none: the area stays house.yaml's (understated, never overstated); the windows have no clear opening to measure

assumptions.what: Bedroom 2's entry alcove (x 366-410, d 146-174) drawn as a room of its own, a room separation line between it and the bedroom
assumptions.why: house.yaml leaves it out (not dimensioned); its size here is what the dimensioned walls around it leave
assumptions.effect: none: bedroom 2's area stays house.yaml's 128.3 sq ft (understated, never overstated)

assumptions.what: Bedroom 2's closet against the east wall
assumptions.why: drawn there on A-3; only its 7'-0" width is dimensioned
assumptions.effect: none: it bounds the alcove only

assumptions.what: C15 and CW14 sizes, and every window's top at 6'-9"
assumptions.why: the codes have no dimensions on the drawings; A-1's general header note
assumptions.effect: none: no window has a clear opening, so no window size is measured

assumptions.what: The bonus room's windows centred in its south wall
assumptions.why: A-3 gives the pair no centre dimension; drawn centred over the bay below

assumptions.what: Second floor: the bridge (7 1/2 in lower), the stairwell and the open areas are drawn on the floor's level, one room with the hallway; the floor slab is drawn whole
assumptions.why: a level per walking surface would split the hall; nothing on them is measured (stairs and guards aren't drawn)

assumptions.what: Main floor: its interior partitions, the living room's bay and the family room's fireplace bump-out aren't drawn; the garage is drawn on the main floor's level
assumptions.why: no main-floor room is in house.yaml and nothing on the main floor but the front door is measured; every extra enclosed area is a chance of one without a Room, which stops every room being read. The garage slab's height disagrees between sheets (README question 10)
assumptions.effect: none on any measure; the front door is in its own wall, as drawn

assumptions.what: Interior doors, the rear sliders, the garage doors and every window not in house.yaml aren't drawn
assumptions.why: house.yaml describes only the front door and the marked escape windows; a drawn door is read as a door of the house
assumptions.effect: none: expected.yaml has only the front door

assumptions.what: The basement as one room in its foundation walls; the unexcavated areas outside it; the basement stair's walls and the mechanical area not drawn
assumptions.why: the basement isn't a sleeping room; its escape windows aren't checked (expected.yaml not_checked)

assumptions.what: The lot (a stand-in rectangle) and its south edge as the street
assumptions.why: Check my project needs a property line and a street edge to send anything
assumptions.effect: none on egress; the Ithaca zoning rows it brings are left out of the comparison

assumptions.what: Every wall drawn 'New', no smoke partition, no fire rating (the build data's own fields)
assumptions.why: the data format needs them; the drawings' house is new construction (A-1 'PROPOSED')
assumptions.effect: none: no rule reads a wall's phase or rating
